prompt: An airline cut fares 10% on one route. Passengers rose 6%, and revenue on the route fell. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Demand on the route is likely price-inelastic, so the cut lost more in price than it gained in volume.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd estimate elasticity from comparable routes.

options.text: It could be elasticity, competitor reactions, the season, capacity or the mix of business and leisure travelers.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: Fare cuts never work, so the airline should never discount.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: The fare cut didn't go as hoped.
options.feedback: This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: A 10% price cut with only 6% more passengers means revenue fell about 5%. The hypothesis explains why and how to check.

distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be elasticity, competitor reactions, the season, capacity or the mix of business and leisure travelers.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: Fare cuts never work, so the airline should never discount.
distractor_flaws.M.untestable_hypothesis: The fare cut didn't go as hoped.
